newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU warns Spain's Telefonica about Antena 3 deal.
newsitem.headline: EU warns Spain's Telefonica about Antena 3 deal.

text.p: The European Commission has warned Spanish telecommunications giant Telefonica de Espana against going ahead with its purchase of a stake in television channel Antena 3 without EU approval.

The planned acquisition was challenged by CanalSatelite, the Spanish digital television platform backed by France's Canal Plus , in the latest round in a fight to control one of Europe's biggest -- and still largely untapped -- pay-TV markets.
The Commission's warning, conveyed in a letter sent to Telefonica's secretary general Jose Mas Millet on Wednesday, comes less than a week before the deal is due to get shareholders' approval.

Following a second complaint from CanalSatelite on August 6 concerning extraordinary meetings of the shareholders of Antena 3 and Audiovisual Sport scheduled for August 18, the Commission warned that any decisions taken could be reversed if necessary.

"In view of what are said to be the consequences for competition of the actions which are apparently planned, I must make it clear that the Commission would not accept being faced with a fait accompli," John Temple Lang, a Commission competition official, said in a letter.
The Commission released the letter after it was leaked in Spain.
The Commission has yet to reach a conclusion on whether Telefonica's planned acquisition of a 25-percent stake in Antena 3 violates European Union competition rules, a Commission spokesman said.

But it was important to inform Telefonica that the deal had been challenged twice by CanalSatelite before it was confirmed next week. "This is a precautionary measure to avoid the irreparable," the spokesman told Reuters.

The battle between the formerly state-controlled Telefonica and CanalSatelite has been raging for months after the telecoms firm announced it would launch its own digital television package called Via Digital.

The dispute spread to the political arena and the Spanish media, with Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar's conservative government allegedly favouring Via Digital and the opposition Socialist Party backing the rival platform. CanalSatelite is jointly controlled by Spanish publishing group Prisa, which owns the influential left-wing newspaper El Pais.

The Commission asked Telefonica to inform the shareholders of Antena 3 and Audiovisual Sport, which has agreed to sell its football broadcast rights to Via Digital, of the complaint and its own investigation by late Thursday.

In a recent surprise move, Telefonica announced it had agreed to buy 25 percent of Antena 3, formerly a key partner in CanalSatelite's digital platform, and to purchase 49 percent of Gestora de Medios Audiovisuales Futbol, Audiovisual's parent.
Spanish banks Santander and BCH have agreed to increase their participation in Antena 3 to 21.57 percent and 21.36 percent respectively on August 18.
The deals do not fall under EU merger rules since the firms realise more than two thirds of their turnover in Spain.
But CanalSatelite argued in two recent complaints that Telefonica was abusing its dominant position in breach of articles 85 and 86 of the EU's founding treaty.
The Commission has not yet decided whether those articles are applicable, but its competition division's first reaction is that "something is not right", a Commission source said.
The Commission could ban or impose strict conditions on the deals if they are found to harm competition.
Telefonica has until September 1 to comment on the substance of the complaint. REUTER
